lane: statistical inverse problems, white noise and sequence models, identifiability, minimax/adaptation, testing and uncertainty

sources.title: Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems
sources.lawful_availability: Complete author-posted arXiv version; publicly accessible.
sources.extraction: MuPDF text extraction of all 34 pages; 76438 extracted characters.
sources.read_extent: Pages 1-34, including appendices A-C and references, read in bounded page chunks.
sources.coverage: Full article; contains linear Gaussian white noise model, posterior Gaussian formula, one-sided feature MAP test, level failure without truth restrictions, regularized test calibration, covariance approximation to optimal probe, source-condition power lower bounds and separation consequence, empirical tuning procedure, and numerical examples. It is an original research article, not the requested lecture notes/textbook.
sources.limits: Does not supply minimax lower bounds, a general adaptive minimax theorem, honest confidence-set coverage, or a full uncertainty quantification theory. One-sample empirical tuning behavior is numerical and expressly lacks theoretical foundation in this article.

sources.title: Statistical inverse problems in active network tomography
sources.lawful_availability: Complete author-posted arXiv version; publicly accessible.
sources.read_extent: Pages 1-21 including references; all read in bounded chunks.
sources.coverage: IMS monograph lecture-note chapter. Applied review of identifiability and probing design for loss and delay tomography; develops parametric delay inference; details EM, moment methods, asymptotic assertions and empirical examples.
sources.limits: Specialized tree-network model, independence and temporal homogeneity assumptions. Cited identifiability results lack full proofs in this chapter; simulations are not general guarantees or confidence-coverage theorems.

sources.title: Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
sources.lawful_availability: Complete main article author-posted on arXiv.
sources.read_extent: Pages 1-26 including references; all read in bounded chunks.
sources.coverage: Gaussian sequence reduction; minimax signal detection for ellipsoidal alternatives, q=2 and sparse q<2; mild/severe/extreme ill-posedness; separation rates, weighted chi-square tests, and adaptive testing.
sources.limits: Detailed proofs are in separate companion supplement DOI 10.1214/12-AOS1011SUPP. Attempts to retrieve Project Euclid paths returned anti-bot HTML; supplement was not obtained or read. Article proof architecture was read, but omitted proof details cannot be claimed.

sources.title: Adaptive minimax optimality in statistical inverse problems via SOLIT -- Sharp Optimal Lepskii-Inspired Tuning
sources.lawful_availability: Complete author-posted arXiv version; publicly accessible.
sources.read_extent: Pages 1-28 including appendix and references; all read in bounded chunks.
sources.coverage: Adaptive minimax MSE for filter-based regularization; SOLIT parameter selection, oracle inequalities, mild and severe ill-posed rate theorems, implementation and simulations.
sources.limits: Estimation/adaptation source, not feature testing or confidence coverage. Severe theorem restricts exponent to 0<theta<=1/2; authors leave stronger adaptation optimality as conjecture in part of regime; super-severe candidate-grid failure is identified.

sources.title: Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions
sources.lawful_availability: Complete author-posted arXiv version; publicly accessible.
sources.read_extent: Pages 1-7 including proof and references; all read.
sources.coverage: General-source ellipsoid minimax estimation theorem; exact cutoff bias-variance risk and constant-factor minimax comparison, with proof and mild/severe examples.
sources.limits: Minimax estimation rather than testing; rate comparison is up to universal constants, not sharp constants.
